git add -A && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(mission): harden C2's read-side default, close two review-probe findings (F2, F3)

C2, completed: ReadActiveMissionBinding's answer for an origin file that
EXISTS but does not cleanly resolve (truncated, or naming a different
mission) was still BindOriginClaim -- positive, contradictory evidence
answered the same as legitimate absence. Round 3's storage split closed
this for every WRITE path in production, but the READ-side default itself
was untouched and its own doc comment still argued for the permissive
answer. Added BindOriginUnknown, a read-only sentinel every Origin-gated
caller (commit_trailers.go, readActiveMissionForDispatch's claim branch)
already refuses by construction. Absence of the origin file is unchanged
and stays BindOriginClaim -- the genuinely safe legacy case.

F2 (review probe): a pending-dispatch entry naming an already-closed
mission was never consumed, and FIFO always re-selects the oldest entry
first -- so one stale entry permanently head-of-line-blocked every newer
pending dispatch for the same Worker. matchDispatchPending now skips and
clears any entry it can PROVE is non-open (a successful Load reporting
non-open status); a Load failure is not treated as proof of anything,
matching C3's doctrine unchanged.

F3 (review probe): two concurrent Agent() spawns in the same session --
not hypothetical, this org's own conventions call for batching independent
tool calls in one turn -- could both match the same oldest pending entry
before either consumed it. dispatchAgent now holds a new per-session
exclusive lock (AcquireDispatchPendingLock) across the entire
match-through-admit-or-fall-back sequence. New lock class, always
acquired outermost, no reversal of any existing acquisition order.

All three confirmed failing pre-fix: C2 via updated assertions on the
existing stale-origin test, F2 and F3 via git stash against the
committed pre-fix code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
